title: A quieter corner of the internet
subtitle: An open-source reading edition
editorNote: This public example brings together the project that inspired Morning Tab and the official building blocks used to make it a native plugin. It is a product reading list, not a claim about today's breaking news.

stories.title: What if your new tab read the internet for you?
stories.summary: AI Homepage explores a personal front page assembled from browsing activity. Its newspaper-style illustration suggests a calmer way to return to the stories you follow: an edited page with a lead, briefings, and real source links.

stories.title: A newspaper that belongs inside the conversation
stories.summary: OpenAI MCP Extensions defines sidebar apps, conversation panels, and native plugin settings. These are the integration points used by Morning Tab's local MCP server.

stories.title: Skills give the tools an editorial workflow
stories.summary: A plugin can bundle skills with its MCP server. Morning Tab uses a skill to guide source reading and attribution, then saves the finished edition through a local tool.

stories.title: The interface starts with a small set of extension APIs
stories.summary: The official TypeScript SDK provides server and app APIs for MCP Extensions. Hosts advertise which optional features they support, so an app can explain when a feature is unavailable.
